title: Locally constant functions on a compact space form a weakly etale algebra
statement: Let T be a compact topological space and R a commutative ring. The ring S = LocallyConstant T R, with its constant-function R-algebra structure and pointwise operations, is weakly etale over R in the ring sense of [def-weil-pbc-ind-etale-algebra]: S is R-flat and S is flat over S tensor_R S via multiplication. No Hausdorff, nonempty or nonzero hypothesis is required.

proof.text: Use the complete existing proof LocallyConstant.weaklyEtale. For completeness, its flatness argument refines any finite family of functions to a finite clopen partition with characteristic functions chi_j. Evaluation at one point in each block trivializes any finite linear relation, which is the equational flatness criterion. For z in the kernel of multiplication S tensor_R S to S, choose such a common partition for a finite sum of pure tensors representing z. The element m = sum_j chi_j tensor chi_j maps to 1 and satisfies m*z = 0: on block j the coefficient is the evaluation of the multiplication of z, hence zero. Multiplication is surjective because f is the image of f tensor 1, and this kernel-annihilation property makes it the localization at the elements mapping to 1. A localization is flat, proving the second flatness condition. The empty space gives S = 0 and the same construction still applies. This node records that closed source proof rather than introducing a new Lean obligation.
